context:
Start by re-confirming the currently pinned DataFusion version still
matches the tested 43.0.0 format (w0) - if it has already drifted, treat
this as more urgent. Land the loud-failure guard (w1) first since it is
small, safe, and immediately converts a silent risk into a visible one.
Only then investigate whether a structural, non-text-parsing alternative
exists in the installed datafusion bindings (w2); if none exists, the loud
guard plus regression test (w1+w3) is an acceptable durable mitigation on
its own.
description:
Architecture review (Work Area E, structural remediation) found that
`benchbox/platforms/dataframe/unified_frame.py:19-23`'s module docstring
self-admits a fragile design: DataFusion support "includes experimental
AST parsing for handling aggregate arithmetic expressions... tested with
DataFusion 43.0.0 and may not work with other versions if the error
message format changes."

The actual mechanism, `_get_datafusion_ast_string()`
(unified_frame.py:2313 onward), deliberately calls
`expr.rex_call_operator()` expecting it to THROW, then parses the AST
representation back out of the exception's string text (comment at
line ~2334: "the error message contains the AST like: 'Catch all
triggered in get_operator_name: Alias(BinaryExpr...)'"). It does a basic
sanity check (`"Alias" in error_str or "BinaryExpr" in error_str or
"AggregateFunction" in error_str`) before trusting the parsed text, and
falls back to passing expressions through unchanged if extraction fails
(per the module docstring) - which can then surface as a downstream
DataFusion error for unsupported aggregate-arithmetic patterns rather than
a clear, attributable failure at the point where the format assumption
broke.

This is a genuine upstream-coupling risk: a DataFusion release that
changes `rex_call_operator()`'s error text format would silently degrade
aggregate-arithmetic support without a clear signal pointing at this file.

anti_patterns.dont: couple the fix to a specific DataFusion patch version
anti_patterns.why: pin the check to the sanity-check keywords and the tested major version documented in the module docstring, so minor version bumps within the same AST-format generation don't spuriously fail.
it is the correct response for genuinely unsupported aggregate-arithmetic patterns (a DataFusion limitation, not a parsing failure); only the format-mismatch branch should become a hard failure.

anti_patterns.dont: silently widen the sanity-check keyword list to accept more error formats speculatively
anti_patterns.why: only change behavior in response to a confirmed installed-version format, verified by w0.

preserves.behavior: Aggregate-arithmetic expressions that currently work correctly against the pinned DataFusion version continue to produce identical results after the hardening change.

The fallback-to-unchanged-expression behavior for genuinely unsupported patterns (not a format-parsing failure) is preserved for cases where DataFusion itself does not support the pattern - only the format-mismatch case should now raise loudly, not every extraction miss.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/platforms/dataframe/unified_frame.py:_get_datafusion_ast_string (2313) and its existing basic sanity check ('Alias'/'BinaryExpr'/'AggregateFunction' in error_str) - reuse and tighten this existing check into a hard assertion rather than adding a parallel validation path.

datafusion-tbl-trailing-delimiter-load.yaml - a prior TODO in this same platform area that replaced ad hoc/fragile per-caller logic with a shared, version-aware helper; follow its pattern of pinning behavior to a documented, tested version and adding a regression test for the failure mode.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests -k 'datafusion and aggregate' --tb=short
verifications.description: Existing DataFusion aggregate-arithmetic tests still pass
New test proves a changed error format now fails loudly instead of silently degrading

work_units.notes:
Installed: DataFusion 53.0.0 (`uv run -- python -c "import datafusion;
print(datafusion.__version__)"`). pyproject.toml's constraint is
`datafusion>=50.1.0` (main `datafusion` extra) with a separate
`datafusion>=40.0.0` floor for an integration-test-only dependency
group. So the version has already drifted well past the
docstring's "tested with 43.0.0" - confirming this is more urgent than
the original Medium priority suggested. Live-probed the actual
rex_call_operator() error text against 53.0.0 for several expression
shapes (plain Column, Literal, unaliased aggregate, aliased
BinaryExpr(AggregateFunction)): the wrapper text
"Catch all triggered in get_operator_name: <ast>" and the
Alias/BinaryExpr/AggregateFunction sanity-check keywords are still
present and structurally unchanged at 53.0.0, so extraction still
works correctly today - but nothing was previously asserting that,
which is exactly the risk w1 addresses.
work_units.summary: Re-validate current DataFusion pinned/installed version against the tested format

work_units.notes:
Implemented in benchbox/platforms/dataframe/unified_frame.py. Added
`DataFusionASTFormatError` and split the failure mode in two instead
of one: (1) if the error text doesn't even contain the stable
"Catch all triggered in get_operator_name" wrapper prefix DataFusion
uses for ALL rex_call_operator() failures regardless of expression
shape (confirmed via live probing in w0), raise
DataFusionASTFormatError naming the installed DataFusion version and
the unrecognized text - this is the actual format-drift case; (2) if
the wrapper prefix IS present but the Alias/BinaryExpr/
AggregateFunction sanity-check keywords are absent, return None as
before - this is a genuinely different/inapplicable expression shape
(e.g. plain Column, Literal, unaliased aggregate), not a format break,
and must_preserve requires this fallback to keep working. Also added
an explicit `hasattr(expr, "rex_call_operator")` guard returning None
for non-Expr objects (e.g. a plain column-name string mixed into the
same select()/agg() call as an aggregate expression) - discovered via
an existing test
(test_unified_lazyframe_datafusion_paths::_DFExpr("SUM(value)")) that
this can legitimately happen and must not be treated as a format
break either.
work_units.summary: Add a version-pinned guard that fails loudly on an unrecognized error format

work_units.notes:
Investigated: the installed datafusion 53.0.0 Python Expr exposes
`to_variant()` (returns a typed object like `datafusion.expr.Alias`
with structured `.alias`/`.expr` attributes, recursively walkable) and
`rex_type()` - genuine structural, non-error-parsing alternatives DO
exist for the currently pinned version. Decided NOT to do the full
replacement in this pass: rewriting
_extract_datafusion_alias_name/_extract_datafusion_multiplier/
_rebuild_datafusion_pure_aggregate/_extract_multi_agg_arithmetic
(which also handles multi-aggregate NVL-wrapped patterns) to walk
to_variant() recursively is a materially larger, higher-regression-risk
rewrite than this TODO's "1-2 days" hardening scope, and the approach
section explicitly permits treating w1+w3 as an acceptable durable
mitigation on their own when a structural replacement isn't done
immediately. Recorded as a follow-up candidate in open_questions
below rather than attempted here.
work_units.summary: Investigate a capability probe or structural API replacing text parsing

work_units.notes:
Added tests/unit/platforms/dataframe/test_unified_frame_datafusion_ast.py
with 6 tests: a changed-wrapper-format case and a
wrapper-missing-entirely case both assert DataFusionASTFormatError
naming the installed datafusion.__version__; a genuinely-different
expression shape and a non-raising expression both assert None
(fallback preserved); a non-Expr object (plain string) asserts None
without raising; and a sanity check that the currently-valid format
still extracts successfully. Also had to fix two PRE-EXISTING tests in
tests/unit/platforms/dataframe/test_unified_frame_coverage.py
(test_get_datafusion_ast_string_success_and_unexpected_error,
test_extract_datafusion_agg_arithmetic_for_literal) whose fake
`rex_call_operator()` messages omitted the real
"Catch all triggered in get_operator_name" wrapper DataFusion actually
uses - under the old code this was harmless (any unrecognized text
just returned None), but under the hardened code it would have
incorrectly raised DataFusionASTFormatError for what are actually
valid/recognized-shape fixtures. Updated the fakes to include the real
wrapper text (matching live-probed DataFusion 53.0.0 behavior) so they
correctly exercise the sanity-check branch rather than the new
format-drift branch. Also added a `rex_call_operator()` method to the
shared `_DFExpr` test double (it previously didn't implement the
method at all, which is why `test_unified_lazyframe_datafusion_paths`
only "worked" by accident under the old silently-permissive code).
work_units.summary: Add a test simulating a changed DataFusion error-message format
